title: Christ in Pietà with Two Angels
medium: Pen and brown ink and brush and brown wash over red chalk on laid paper
medium_parts: Pen and brown ink and brush and brown wash over red chalk on laid paper
identifying_description: Christ being taken from the tomb by the angel behind him, with Mary at right holding his left arm, hill behind them with a skull sitting on top
web_text: In this poignant depiction of human suffering, Christ’s lifeless body sinks into one angel’s shoulder as another angel surrounds him with open arms. Trometta delimited these figures in lively curvilinear pen-and-ink lines over a preliminary drawing made in red chalk. The artist sculpted Christ’s body by applying wash to mimic shadow and convey a sense of volume. Drawn in Rome in the midst of the sixteenth-century Counter-Reformation, this rendering of Christ’s suffering would have been used to inspire contemplation and piety in Christian viewers—a sentiment echoed by the position of the angel at right, whose head (as the reworked passage reveals) was reoriented by the artist from looking down to instead gazing upon the face of Jesus.
